title: Stage Cue Groomer and Bandwidth-Aware Prefetch Arbiter for Multi-GPU Scheduling
creator: Riley Chen
description:
Summary: Implement a lightweight stage-cue mechanism ("cues") and a bandwidth-aware prefetch arbiter to improve NCCL overlap and kernel selection coordination across tensor and pipeline parallel stages. Goal is to reduce p99 prefill and decode tail latency, smooth NCCL traffic, and enable opportunistic kernel variants without regressing throughput.

Background: Current multi-GPU runs show variance spikes when NCCL collectives are scheduled naively at stage boundaries; compute stalls and overloaded interconnect windows increase latency during bursty workloads. We need a pragmatic runtime-level controller that: 1) signals upcoming communication intention early via micro-cues, 2) reserves adaptive NCCL windows shaped by measured link bandwidth and outstanding work, and 3) negotiates kernel variants (attention chunking, fused matmul-kernel, quantization-friendly path) that trade latency vs bandwidth.

Proposed design:
- Stage Cue Groomer: a tiny, per-request metadata token emitted at prefill/decode boundaries that carries: estimated token-count-to-send, preferred kernel profile hint (latency/throughput), and a soft deadline. Cues are piggybacked on RPC metadata or inserted into per-node lightweight queue to avoid new IPC IPC costs.
- Bandwidth-Aware Prefetch Arbiter: a centralized (per-worker) policy that consumes cues and current link telemetry to decide: prefetch size (microbatch grouping), NCCL rendezvous time-window, and whether to use overlapping or deferred collectives. The arbiter uses EWMA of link utilization and a saturating estimator for outstanding comms.
- Kernel election API: extend existing kernel hints so the arbiter can request a low-latency attention kernel (small-chunk fused attention), a bandwidth-friendly chunked attention kernel, or an aggressive quantized path. Hints are advisory; kernel fallback remains local.

Trade-offs and constraints:
- Complexity: keep cue packets minimal to avoid added scheduling jitter. Avoid global consensus; the arbiter is per-worker with soft coordination via short-lived leases.
- Safety: never delay collectives beyond a conservative bound; add a hard timeout that forces immediate NCCL call to avoid correctness regressions.
- Observability: add telemetry for cue delay, reserved window size, lost-overlap events, and per-kernel choice counts.

Success metrics:
- 95th/99th prefill+decode tail latency reduction target: >=20% relative to baseline for mixed short/long prompts.
- End-to-end throughput unaffected (within 5%) for steady-state high-throughput workloads.
- Decrease in NCCL-congestion events (retries/timeouts) by 30%.

Testing plan:
- Microbenchmarks: synthetic token-wave tests across homogeneous and heterogeneous GPU meshes (NVLink-rich and NVSwitch).
- Staging: run canary with 5% traffic on dedicated pool; enable detailed tracing and guardrails.
- Safety rollback: automatic disable if p99 latency increases or error rates rise above threshold.

Implementation milestones:
1) Spec and proto (2 days): finalize cue fields, telemetry events, kernel hint enums.
2) Arbiter prototype (5 days): per-worker controller, simple EWMA bandwidth estimator, decision rules.
3) Kernel hint plumbing (3 days): wire hint through runtime to kernel selector with safe fallback.
4) Integration tests and canary (4 days): perf harness, dashboards, rollback hooks.

Rollout plan: start with internal dedicated cluster for prefills only, then expand to decode traffic if stable. Add a feature flag that allows forcing specific kernel variants for debugging.

Open questions:
- Best quantization-friendly kernel handoff latency threshold? Proposal: prefer quantized path when expected tokens > 256 and link utilization > 70%.
- Lease duration for arbiter coordination: default 50ms, tunable per-topology.

Notes: This ticket is intentionally conservative: the arbiter suggests hints; final kernel selection remains local to each device to preserve determinism and fallbacks.

Links to artifacts: design doc, perf dashboard, and prototype PR attached below.
